markdown.markdown:
::: {.callout-note} Welcome, students! This specialized academic portal provides in-depth resources for the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) curriculum. Here, you will find exhaustive syllabus checklists, revision notes, targeted practice question banks, and official exam information—all mathematically formatted to optimize your learning and help you achieve a Grade 9. ::: ## 1 Course Introduction

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) is a structured and comprehensive academic curriculum designed to develop mathematical skills, logical thinking, and problem-solving capabilities. The syllabus is divided into two tiers of entry: Foundation Tier (grades 5–1) and Higher Tier (grades 9–4, with grade 3 allowed), offering appropriate routes of assessment for students of different abilities.

### Assessment Outline
Paper Number Tier Assessment Information Marks Weighting
Paper 1F Foundation Assessed through a 2-hour examination set and marked by Pearson. The paper is weighted at 50% of the qualification, targeted at grades 5–1. Calculator allowed. 100 marks 50%
Paper 2F Foundation Assessed through a 2-hour examination set and marked by Pearson. The paper is weighted at 50% of the qualification, targeted at grades 5–1. Calculator allowed. 100 marks 50%
Paper 1H Higher Assessed through a 2-hour examination set and marked by Pearson. The paper is weighted at 50% of the qualification, targeted at grades 9–4 with 3 allowed. Calculator allowed. 100 marks 50%
Paper 2H Higher Assessed through a 2-hour examination set and marked by Pearson. The paper is weighted at 50% of the qualification, targeted at grades 9–4 with 3 allowed. Calculator allowed. 100 marks 50%
**Assessment Objectives (AOs) Weightings:** * **AO1 (Number and algebra):** 57 - 63% * **AO2 (Shape, space and measures):** 22 - 28% * **AO3 (Handling data):** 12 - 18% ### Syllabus Structure

The Edexcel IGCSE Mathematics A syllabus content is categorized into 6 major topics, covering core concepts for all students with extended high-level parts for the Higher Tier:

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## 1 Numbers and the number system **1.1** Integers
**1.2** Fractions
**1.3** Decimals
**1.4** Powers and roots
**1.5** Set language and notation
**1.6** Percentages
**1.7** Ratio and proportion
**1.8** Degree of accuracy
**1.9** Standard form
**1.10** Applying number
**1.11** Electronic calculators
::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## 2 Equations, formulae and identities **2.1** Use of symbols
**2.2** Algebraic manipulation
**2.3** Expressions and formulae
**2.4** Linear equations
**2.5** Proportion (Higher Tier only)
**2.6** Simultaneous linear equations
**2.7** Quadratic equations
